scope: checksum-verification amendment to the source-only portion (migration 343 edited in place, provisional, applied nowhere); the hosted Storage proof (acceptance item 3) stays outside this review and open
method: Two independent read-only reviewers on the uncommitted tree of codex/hfo-col143-evidence. SQL: the amended 343, its probe, the stub change and the race script, with rolled-back experiments on the run-owned native cluster against col143_chk343 (amended stack) and col143_base343 (old stack, before its rebuild). TypeScript: md5.ts verified independently against Node crypto for lengths 0..300, padding boundaries, multi-chunk and 512 MiB+1 inputs; evidence library, three routes and tests against the 343 reply shapes and RAISE wordings. Both ran the gates. Every finding was dispositioned and remediated before the commit; the SQL reviewer re-verified the remediation.

sql_review.verdict: changes requested (no blocker; two should-fix, five notes) → re-verified PASS after remediation

findings.where: col143-evidence/concurrency.txt and the race script's default baseline
findings.claim: the recorded race evidence predated the amendment and its baseline database still carried the old 343 (no declared_md5, no storage.objects.version), so the amended race script would fail deterministically there
findings.disposition: Fixed: col143_base343 dropped and rebuilt from the amended stack; race script re-run (three cases PASS with observed lock waits); concurrency.txt regenerated with a timestamped header naming the baseline; re-verified by the reviewer against the rebuilt database.

findings.claim: the eTag is client-unwritable only while storage.objects is reachable solely through the Storage service: a direct INSERT with a crafted eTag passes the insert policy (UPDATE and DELETE affect zero rows), harmless only because the storage schema is not API-exposed
findings.disposition: Documented as the trust-anchor precondition in §1 and §6; hosted proof step 0 added: confirm storage is absent from the project's exposed API schemas (expected public, graphql_public) with a stop rule.

findings.claim: the checksum_mismatch failed event carried a NULL expected receipt revision while object_changed and finalized events carry it
findings.disposition: Fixed: the shared step takes p_expected_revision; mark passes NULL, finalize passes the caller's expected revision; probe asserts both (158 assertions).

findings.claim: a re-formatted eTag with the same normalised MD5 and same id/version still finalizes; finalize-from-prepared observes the object once; the version must match only when one was recorded
findings.disposition: Wording added to the contract and the spec.
